      MonoVLM: Monocular 3D Visual Grounding with Vision Language Models

                        Huaizhi Qu1,2 , Hossein Nourkhiz Mahjoub2 , Vaishnav Tadiparthi2 ,
                                           Kwonjoon Lee2 , Tianlong Chen1
                     1
                       University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, 2 Honda Research Institute USA
                                      {huaizhiq, tianlong}@cs.unc.edu

                                                                                         (b) Performance comparison

Figure 1. We propose MonoVLM, a simple yet effective method to equip Vision-Language Models (VLMs) with robust monocular 3D
grounding capabilities. (a) The model takes an image and the textual query to predict the 3D bounding box (GT and prediction). (b) Even
the latest large-scale VLMs struggle to understand 3D structure from 2D images. Our resulting model not only achieves significantly better
results than these VLMs but also surpasses specialized vision-only models designed for this task.


                                  Abstract                                 performance of specialized vision-only models. We validate
                                                                           our design via extensive comparisons and ablation studies.

Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated remark-
able capabilities in instruction following and 2D visual un-               1. Introduction
derstanding. However, state-of-the-art VLMs, including
GPT-5, still struggle with 3D perception, particularly in                 The ability to comprehend the three-dimensional world from
tasks such as monocular 3D visual grounding. While spe-                   two-dimensional images is a fundamental goal in computer
cialized vision-only models excel in this domain, they often              vision and a critical component for a vast array of appli-
lack the rich semantic understanding inherent to VLMs. To                 cations, including robotics [6, 15, 17, 25], 3D scene un-
bridge this gap, we propose MonoVLM, a novel triple-stage                 derstanding [10, 20, 30, 34, 42], and autonomous driving
training framework that enables VLMs to perform accurate                  [14, 35, 36]. In pursuit of this goal, the field has seen re-
monocular 3D grounding. The core of our method is a pro-                  markable progress, with specialized, task-oriented architec-
gressive training process that uses Group Relative Policy                 tures delivering superhuman performance on specific bench-
Optimization (GRPO) to gradually teach the model to first lo-             marks such as monocular 3D object detection or grounding
calize the described object, then understand its 3D structure,            [7, 11, 19, 32, 38–41]. However, these expert models of-
and finally estimate the full 3D bounding box accurately.                 ten lack the flexibility to handle diverse tasks beyond their

VLMs to improve their capability on complex tasks. In par-         Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). We op-
ticular, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) [22] has        timize our model using Group Relative Policy Optimiza-
proven effective for stabilizing the training of large models      tion (GRPO) [22], a recent reinforcement learning algorithm
by optimizing them directly for task-specific rewards, such        that has demonstrated strong performance in training Large
as 2D localization accuracy. Recent studies have demon-            Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models
strated that applying GRPO to 2D visual grounding tasks            (VLMs). GRPO is particularly well-suited for tasks with ver-
significantly improves performance, reasoning, and out-of-         ifiable reward metrics, such as the Intersection over Union
distribution generalization compared to standard supervised        (IoU) in visual grounding. Unlike traditional policy gradient
fine-tuning [5, 23, 44]. The success of RL-based optimiza-         methods like PPO [21], which require an additional critic
tion in sharpening 2D grounding skills provides strong moti-       model to estimate policy performance, GRPO directly com-
vation for applying similar reward-driven strategies to tackle     pares a group of candidate responses to assess their relative
the greater complexities of monocular 3D visual grounding.         quality, eliminating the need for a separate critic.

Figure 2. Overview of the MonoVLM framework, which employs a coarse-to-fine, three-stage GRPO training curriculum. Stage 1 establishes
robust 2D visual grounding. Stage 2 builds on this by training the model to predict the 3D object center, learning the 2D-to-3D mapping.
Finally, Stage 3 optimizes for the complete 3D bounding box by using a composite reward signal that combines the overall 3D IoU with
fine-grained, parameter-specific rewards. Please zoom in for better visualization of the GT and prediction.

   distance. While the 2D grounding IoU is not part of the training objective in this stage, it shows collateral improvement. This demonstrates a
   strong synergy between the 2D and 3D localization tasks, suggesting that the model discovers the duality between 2D and 3D.
